records.text: i am ailmzx48 a local conversational language model for the 48k sinclair zx spectrum
spectrum is a 1982 home computer by sinclair research using a z80a processor with 16k rom and 16k or 48k ram
spectrum history begins in 1982 after the zx81 and later includes plus and 128k models
48k spectrum memory combines 16k rom and 48k ram in the z80 64k address space
ailmzx48 runs locally on the machine and does not require a network service for conversation
classic spectrum games include manic miner jet set willy and knight lore
the original spectrum was sold with either 16k or 48k ram
the spectrum display is 256 by 192 pixels with colour attributes arranged in 8 by 8 character cells
the original spectrum uses a rubber keyboard and cassette tape for common program storage
the spectrum ula handles video timing memory contention and much of the machine interface logic
sinclair basic is stored in the spectrum 16k rom
the spectrum followed the zx81 in the sinclair home computer line
the spectrum plus appeared after the original rubber keyboard model
later spectrum models expanded memory beyond the original 48k configuration
the spectrum became an important british home computer for games programming and education
the 48k spectrum screen area occupies 6912 bytes including bitmap and colour attribute data
the display bitmap uses 6144 bytes and the colour attribute area uses 768 bytes
careful memory use matters because code graphics data stack and runtime state must share limited ram
bounded buffers and fixed tables help software remain predictable on a 48k machine
local conversation keeps model execution on the spectrum side of the zx ux environment
offline chat avoids dependence on a remote language model service
bounded local inference trades model size for predictable memory and execution cost
manic miner is a platform game associated with matthew smith and the spectrum
jet set willy followed manic miner and became another well known spectrum platform game
knight lore is known for an isometric presentation that influenced later home computer games
games helped define the spectrum software scene and encouraged bedroom programming
i am ailmzx48 a local language model made for conversation
i am ailmzx48 and i answer with small clear replies
i am local and careful about what i know
small models should prefer clear useful answers over confident guessing
spectrum hardware rewards simple explanations and precise facts
spectrum is a compact home computer with a memorable design
history is easiest to follow when dates and model changes stay clear
spectrum history starts in 1982 and grows through later models
memory matters because every byte deserves care
memory pressure rewards careful software design
48k memory feels generous only until code data and graphics all need space
local chat runs without a network
local conversation keeps the machine self contained
games are part of spectrum culture
games gave spectrum much of its character
classic games show how much personality can fit in a small computer
the 48k spectrum screen bitmap occupies addresses 16384 through 22527
the spectrum colour attribute memory occupies addresses 22528 through 23295
the 48k spectrum system variables begin at address 23552 decimal
the 48k spectrum rom occupies addresses 0 through 16383 and ram occupies 16384 through 65535
the spectrum z80a processor runs at about 3500000 hz or three point five mhz
the spectrum ula io port 254 controls border colour and also carries beeper and cassette signals
the spectrum keyboard is an eight by five matrix read through the ula by selecting keyboard rows
spectrum basic programs and their variables are held in ram while the basic interpreter is held in rom
spectrum basic peek reads the value of a byte at an address and poke writes a value to a byte at an address
spectrum basic randomize usr followed by an address calls a machine code routine at that address
spectrum basic clear with a numeric address can change ramtop so bytes above the new ramtop can be preserved for machine code
spectrum basic new deletes the current basic program and variables before starting the basic system anew
spectrum basic save and load store and retrieve programs using cassette tape on the original machine
spectrum basic run clears variables and starts program execution from the first line or a specified line
spectrum basic program lines are listed in ascending line number order
reading spectrum ula port 254 uses bit 6 for the ear cassette input signal
writing spectrum ula port 254 bit 4 drives the ear output and internal speaker while bit 3 drives the mic output
a kempston joystick interface is read at io port 31 and uses active high direction and fire bits
sinclair interface 2 joysticks appear as spectrum number keys 1 through 5 and 6 through 0
the kempston joystick interface plugs into the spectrum rear edge expansion connector
cassette tape was the primary storage medium for the original spectrum and used the ear and mic connections
zx spectrum launched 23 april 1982 at 125 pounds for 16k and 175 pounds for 48k
spectrum plus arrived in 1984 with ql style keyboard reset button and 48k ram
spectrum 128 reached britain in january 1986 with 128k ram and three channel ay sound after spanish investronica development
amstrad acquired spectrum computer rights in april 1986 and continued the line
spectrum plus 2 was the first amstrad spectrum in 1986 with a built in cassette deck
spectrum plus 3 arrived in 1987 with a built in three inch floppy disk drive
the hobbit was a 1982 melbourne house text adventure for zx spectrum and sold over 500000 units in europe
jetpac was a 1983 ultimate play the game shoot em up for the 16k spectrum
ant attack was a 1983 quicksilva game associated with sandy white and used isometric 3d graphics
skool daze was a 1984 microsphere game associated with david reidy
head over heels was a 1987 ocean game associated with jon ritman and bernie drummond using isometric 3d graphics
saboteur was a 1985 durell software game associated with clive townsend
the c48 sdk is the portable host side development kit for spectrum c48 programs while future native zx ux cc remains separate
c48 is the command line compiler front end in the spectrum c48 sdk
c48run is the portable host runtime and virtual machine for c48 programs
c48 int and unsigned int values use two bytes and c48 pointers are also two bytes
c48 uses a 16 bit logical address space of 64 kibibytes
c48 float storage uses five byte spectrum style representation
c48b1 is a deterministic sdk host executable and is not zx ux obj1 mex1 or z80 machine code
c48 sources under usr src compile by default to the matching relative path under usr bin
the c48 sdk software text mode is 64 columns by 24 rows using a four by eight font
c48run headless mode can dump the exact deterministic 6912 byte spectrum screen state
